commands.help: Deterministic policy checks backing ops/cio-sidecar-brief.md.

Check one proposal against the brief's mechanical rules and print a verdict.

This is the mechanical half of the sidecar's own judgment, not a
replacement for it: `claude-cio` (or any session reading
ops/cio-sidecar-brief.md) runs this before approving/rejecting/escalating
a plan, so the parts of the brief that are a fixed rule - a self-approval
check, a spend cap, a prohibited category - are enforced the same way
every time instead of re-derived from a vibe. Exits 0 with JSON always;
the verdict field carries approve/reject/escalate.

parameters.name: decider
parameters.help: Identity about to render the verdict (e.g. claude-cio).

parameters.name: category
parameters.help: Repeatable; a policy category the proposal touches.

Start BitCadence quietly in the background (the pair of 'mco stop').

No window stays open: the gateway runs hidden, a small status icon appears
near the clock, and the app opens already signed in. Unlike 'mco serve'
(foreground, for terminals/systemd/Docker), your terminal stays free. Output
goes to ~/.mco/logs/gateway.log and 'mco stop' shuts it down.
